detail: Negative 7 said Leonard Aubrey Robert Wear does not appear in the England and Wales probate calendar for 1973. It rested on a zero from the wrong half of the service, and this archive then published two further wrong accounts of why. THE CALENDAR HAS NOW ACTUALLY BEEN READ, for four years instead of one, and the negative holds — this time on evidence.

probatesearch.service.gov.uk answers in two halves. The DIGITAL half indexes only grants issued from 1996, so any pre-1996 query returns zero before a search happens. The IMAGE half calls an OCR endpoint, pp_cowindex_default_search, over the scanned calendar cut into page-sized chunks, EACH FILE NAMED FOR THE FIRST SURNAME ON IT — 009223_weake_1973.pdf runs from Weake to Weare. The chunk's OCR text comes back as a property, textract:docContent, so the page never has to be rendered at all.

finding: *** AND THE COUNT PRINTED ON THE RESULTS PAGE IS A DEFECT — IGNORE IT ***
detail: The page says "41 document pages returned" for Wear 1973, for Smith 1973, for Luwinski, for the nonsense string Zqxvwyrk, for 1979, with a forename and with a keyword. Called directly the same searches return 41, 469, 0, 0. THE DISPLAYED NUMBER IS NOT THE NUMBER OF RESULTS, and two of this archive's three wrong answers came from believing it.

finding: # ---------------- THE CONTROLS, RUN FIRST THIS TIME ----------------

detail: Ernest Leslie in 1973 returns EIGHTEEN chunks — a forename pair read off the Wear block itself, so the instrument is demonstrably finding text this archive can see with its own eyes.
WEAR 1973 returns 41 chunks, SMITH 1973 returns 469, LUWINSKI returns 0. The count MOVES WITH THE NAME, which is the whole test the earlier attempts skipped.

finding: 1973 — EIGHT WEAR GRANTS, AND NO LEONARD
detail: ALFRED of 21 Ash St, Crosshills, Yorks · DOROTHY WINIFRED of 44 The Glebe, Minchinhampton · ELLEN of Willow Cottage, Robin Rd, Summerseat, Bury · ELSIE of 26 Mandale Rd, Horton Bank Top, Bradford · ERNEST LESLIE of 9 Valley Gdns, Gateshead · JAMES WATSON of 1 Richardson St, Ashington · MARY ROSINE of 42 Enys Rd, Eastbourne · WILLIAM of 432 Kings Dv, Wembley. Read from 009223_weake_1973.pdf, which runs Weake to Weare and therefore contains the whole of WEAR.

finding: 1974 — ONE, and it is not him
detail: WALTER of 3 Hallgarth, Airton, Skipton. From 009474_wear_1974.pdf.
JAMES WILLIAM of 536 Plessey Rd, Blyth · ARTHUR of Woodside House, Wrotham Rd, Meopham · CHARLES of 21 Downsway, Great Bookham · EDITH MAUD of 47 Broomhill Rd, Broomhill. From 008820_weale_1979.pdf.
ANNIE ELLEN of 64 Surbiton Rd, Southend-on-Sea · NORMAN of Willow Cottage, Robin Rd, Summerseat · ROSETTA EMMA of St Augustines, Addlestone. From 009151_wear_1980.pdf.

finding: why 1974 and 1980 were read at all
detail: *** THE CALENDAR IS ORDERED BY YEAR OF GRANT, NOT YEAR OF DEATH. *** The 1973 volume contains people who died in December 1972. So a death in 1973 can be granted in 1974, and a death in 1979 granted in 1980, and reading only the two candidate years would have left exactly the gap this archive keeps falling into. Both following years were read for that reason.

finding: *** AND THE WIDER TEST, WHICH IS THE STRONGER ONE ***
detail: The forename pair "LEONARD AUBREY" was put to the OCR for EVERY YEAR FROM 1970 TO 1981. It returns TWENTY-SIX MEN. Their surnames are BRICKNELL · DINSMORE · WILLIAMS · DAY · HILL · BENISTON · MOORE · BARTON · PETERS · WAGHORNE · EVANS · HOGBEN · PRIDOLE · WEBBERLEY · HOWARD · BRIERS (four times) · COOPER · HILLIER · PALMER · HAWKINS · WINES · BRIGHT · STUCKEY. *** NOT ONE OF THEM IS A WEAR. *** Twelve years of the calendar, searched on the forenames rather than the surname, and he is not in it.

finding: # ---------------- WHAT IT IS WORTH, AND WHAT IT IS NOT ----------------

detail: NO GRANT OF PROBATE OR ADMINISTRATION WAS MADE IN ENGLAND AND WALES TO A LEONARD AUBREY WEAR BETWEEN 1970 AND 1981, and the sixteen Wear grants of 1973, 1974, 1979 and 1980 have been read name by name.

It says nothing about where he died. An English grant needs English assets, and a man who died in South Africa need never appear here at all — so this is a negative about a route, not about a life. IT ALSO RESTS ON OCR: a badly scanned line is invisible to the query, and this corpus prints "Milliam" for William and "Minifred" for Winifred on the very page that was read. THAT IS WHY THE SURNAME BLOCKS WERE READ IN FULL RATHER THAN SEARCHED — the eight 1973 entries were counted off the page, not returned by a query.
